title: One Obstruction, Three Faces — Merle Lean stack, with Lean 4 formalisations of Halbeisen–Hungerbühler 1997 and Lagarias 1990
description:
Lean 4 verification stack of Eric Merle (the “kernel key”) for the joint note One obstruction, three faces with Benjamin Macindoe, together with Lean 4 formalisations of two classical papers: L. Halbeisen and N. Hungerbühler, “Optimal bounds for the length of rational Collatz cycles”, Acta Arithmetica 78 (1997), 227–239, and J. C. Lagarias, “The set of rational cycles for the 3x+1 problem”, Acta Arithmetica 56 (1990), 33–53.

hh1997/ (Lean 4.34.0, Mathlib v4.34.0): every result that the paper proves is kernel-checked (70 proved statements, each frozen before its proof was written), with no sorry in the proofs, no native_decide, and only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. One statement of the paper, Remark 1 for l > 10³, is stated and not proved, since the paper gives no proof; Remark 2 and two figures the paper quotes from other authors are not formalised. The formalisation proves nothing new about Collatz cycles. See hh1997/README.md, which also lists the points found in the paper.

lagarias1990/ (Lean 4.34.0, Mathlib v4.34.0): 59 proved statements, each frozen before its proof was written, with no sorry in the proofs, no native_decide, and only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Theorem 3.1 with the printed constant and Theorem 3.2 are proved under named hypotheses (the prime number theorem; the Baker–Fel’dman bound (3.3)), which are hypotheses of the theorems, not axioms; Theorem 3.1 is also proved without any hypothesis, with the constant 6/5 instead of 5/4. Theorems 3.3 and 4.3 are out of scope. Where a printed statement or proof has a slip, the repaired version is proved and the slip is listed next to what is printed in lagarias1990/README.md. The formalisation proves nothing new about Collatz cycles.

The rest of the repository is the Merle side of the joint note; the status of each of its entries is the claims ledger of the shared repository macindoe/one-obstruction-three-faces, not this archive. Its six Lean files were first checked on Lean 4.27.0 and re-checked on Lean 4.34.0 (recheck-v4.34/RECHECK.md). Nothing in this repository excludes a Collatz cycle beyond the published bounds (Bařina's verification to 2^71; Hercher 2023).
